extracted.intended_audience: employers, attorneys, economists, policymakers, and public commenters participating in FTC rulemaking on non-compete agreements
extracted.subtask_description: Guidance and evidentiary standards used by the FTC in evaluating non-compete agreements and comments submitted to the agency's rulemaking on non-competes. Focuses on empirical-evidence standards, scope/exceptions (including senior executives and highly compensated employees), and related measurement approaches.

rubrics_metrics.name: Principles for robust design (Part IV.A.2)
rubrics_metrics.description: Principles for robust empirical design outlined in Part IV.A.2 (the Commission evaluates whether studies satisfy these metrics).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Referenced repeatedly as the guideposts the Commission uses to weigh empirical studies. The text notes some studies satisfy 'each of the other metrics outlined in Part IV.A.2' while others 'satisfy some of the principles for robust design outlined in Part IV.A.2' but have limitations. See Part IV.A.2 for the full list of metrics (sample representativeness, identification, appropriate outcome measures, etc.).

rubrics_metrics.name: Outcome alignment: use outcome measures that match the economic question
rubrics_metrics.description: The Commission notes that average per-firm employment does not precisely correspond to the economic outcome of interest, which is overall employment or job creation.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: When evaluating empirical work, ensure the reported outcome metric directly corresponds to the policy question (e.g., job creation should be measured as overall employment/job creation rather than average per-firm employment). Studies that use proxies that do not align with the economic outcome may be given less weight.

rubrics_metrics.name: Measurement of enforceability should be nuanced (avoid crude binary indicators)
rubrics_metrics.description: The Commission identifies allegedly flawed measures that use binary indicators for enforcement versus non-enforcement or for several facets of enforceability, and contrasts those with more nuanced measures.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Prefer measures that capture gradations of enforceability rather than simple enforcement/non-enforcement binaries. The Commission cites older studies using binary indicators as flawed and references more nuanced, recent measures (e.g., Bishara).

rubrics_metrics.name: Attenuation bias: account for measurement error in independent variables
rubrics_metrics.description: Attenuation bias occurs when the independent variable (here, whether a worker is covered by the ban) is measured with error.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Empirical analyses should consider how measurement error in key independent variables biases estimated effects (typically toward zero), and implement methods or robustness checks to address attenuation bias.

rubrics_metrics.name: Concentration measurement: employment-based Herfindahl-Hirschman Index (HHI)
rubrics_metrics.description: Concentration is measured by an employment-based Herfindahl-Hirschman Index (HHI).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Use employment shares (rather than, e.g., establishments or revenues) to calculate HHI when assessing labor-market concentration effects related to non-competes, as the Commission cites studies using employment-based HHI.

rubrics_metrics.name: Highly compensated employee threshold (85th percentile)
rubrics_metrics.description: This threshold is based on the 85th percentile of earnings of full-time salaried workers nationally.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: The Commission uses an earnings threshold tied to the 85th percentile of full-time salaried worker earnings to define 'highly compensated' workers for purposes of coverage/exceptions; the rule and analysis reference prior DOL/IRS thresholds and state statutes for context.

rubrics_metrics.name: Consideration of rescission of existing non-competes (proposed § 910.2(b)(1))
rubrics_metrics.description: Because the Commission proposed to require employers to rescind existing non-competes—see NPRM, proposed § 910.2(b)(1)—many comments addressed the proposed rescission requirement specifically.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Comments that pertain only to rescission are addressed separately (Part IV.E); the Commission treats rescission-specific issues distinct from general coverage/exceptions analysis. Rule drafters and commenters should separately analyze rescission impacts and legal/operational implications.

rubrics_metrics.name: Primary focus on direct negative effects on product and service market competition
rubrics_metrics.description: The Commission focuses on the most direct negative effects on competition in product and service markets in this Part IV.B.3.b; inefficient matching between workers and firms may have additional negative effects, including on output.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: When assessing competitive harm from non-competes, the Commission prioritizes direct effects on product/service market competition, while recognizing labor-market frictions (e.g., inefficient matching) can have secondary negative effects.

rubrics_metrics.name: Evidence standard for claims about exploitation/coercion: require underlying data
rubrics_metrics.description: The Commission found news reports that 'did not include the underlying data used for the evaluation' and considered such reports 'insufficient evidence at this time to find exploitation and coercion' for a subset of senior executives.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Claims of exploitation, coercion, or similar harms require supporting underlying data; anecdotal or journalistic reports without data are given insufficient weight for formal findings.

rubrics_metrics.name: Consider prevalence and interaction of related contractual provisions
rubrics_metrics.description: High prevalence of co-occurring provisions: e.g., 97.5% of workers with non-competes are also subject to a non-solicitation agreement, NDA, or a non-recruitment agreement, and 74.7% are subject to all three provisions.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Analyses and rule design should account for related contractual terms (non-solicitation, confidentiality/NDAs, non-recruitment) because their prevalence affects the net restrictiveness of agreements and the interpretation of impacts attributed to non-competes alone.

rubrics_metrics.name: Consideration of other relevant legal thresholds and definitions (FLSA, DOL, IRS, state law)
rubrics_metrics.description: The Commission references FLSA, DOL proposed thresholds, IRS definitions, and state statutes (e.g., DC Code) when discussing coverage/exceptions and thresholds for highly compensated employees.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Rulemaking should take into account other federal and state statutory definitions and thresholds (e.g., highly compensated employee tests, state-specific bans/limits) and explain how the rule interacts with or differs from those standards.

rubrics_metrics.name: Sufficiency of evidence categories: new business formation and innovation
rubrics_metrics.description: The Commission finds that the effects of non-competes on new business formation and innovation, standing alone, are sufficient to sustain its finding that non-competes tend to negatively affect competitive conditions in product and service markets.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Evidence showing substantial adverse effects on new business formation or innovation can independently support a finding that non-competes harm competition; rulemaking analysis should separately assess each of these outcome categories.

rubrics_metrics.name: Weighting of single-study results relative to methodological shortcomings
rubrics_metrics.description: The Commission notes some studies are given less weight because they consider only one change in enforceability, restrict to particular geographies, or have sample restrictions that limit generalizability.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: When evaluating empirical claims in comments, consider study design limitations (single policy change, narrow sample, industry restriction) and reduce weight accordingly; robust inference requires broader generalizability or stronger identification.
